children: The generated Postgres tsvector that Postgres Search ranks against — weighted by field and indexed for speed.
on the Document table holding a tsvector assembled with setweight:
| Weight | Field(s) | |---|---| | A | title | | B | author + category | | C | slug | | D | body |

The weight classes are what give Postgres Search its "title beats body" behaviour — ts_rank reads them when scoring, and the recent relevance fix that weights title above body in the vector lives right here.
over the column makes full-text lookups fast across the whole corpus. Phrase queries (via phraseto_tsquery) and the exact-title boost both resolve against this same indexed vector.
Because the column is GENERATED, its definition is fixed at DDL time — you cannot mutate the weights in place. Changing the setweight recipe means a Migration that
the column, which recomputes the vector for every existing row. That is the lever used whenever the field-weight policy changes.

The Indx Engine does not touch search_vector at all — it maintains its own index and ranks with BM25F. The two engines reach comparable field weighting by different roads, both sitting behind the single Search contract and feeding the same Search Facets. Note the Auto Correction Loop's Synonyms expansion happens before the vector is queried, so learned corrections match against it cleanly. Vector quality is scored by the Golden Eval harness, and any future tuning of these weight classes would train on the clickstream in Search Intelligence.
